title: kate-text: EditLog, Anchor, revision-to-revision offset transform
summary: Positions that survive edits without an observer pattern. An Anchor is a Copy value (offset, revision, bias). The buffer keeps a log of applied transactions back to the oldest locked revision and resolves an anchor by replaying the log. This single mechanism replaces KTextEditor's MovingCursor, MovingRange and TextHistory::transformCursor.

lane.reason: Pure algorithmic work on kate-text with property tests; no platform dependency.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: TextBuffer gains a private EditLog field and six public methods. Nothing existing changes shape. Unlocked history older than the oldest lock is dropped; resolving an anchor older than that is an error, not a guess.

regression_tests.name: anchor::tests::anchor_after_edit_resolves_to_shifted_offset
regression_tests.asserts: An anchor at offset 10 resolves to 13 after inserting three chars at offset 4, and to 10 after inserting at offset 20.

regression_tests.name: anchor::tests::bias_decides_insert_at_anchor
regression_tests.asserts: Insert exactly at the anchor: Bias::Left keeps the offset, Bias::Right moves past the inserted text.

regression_tests.name: anchor::tests::resolve_equals_eager_tracking
regression_tests.asserts: For random edit sequences, resolving an anchor through the log equals applying transform_offset eagerly after each edit. Fixed seed.

regression_tests.name: log::tests::unlocked_history_is_pruned_and_stale_is_an_error
regression_tests.asserts: Without a lock, resolving an anchor from revision 0 after 2 edits is Err(StaleAnchor); with lock_revision(0) it is Ok.
